name: Palawan
tagline: Turtles, secret lagoons and a pyramid in the sea
summary: The wildest corner of the Philippines: jungle-cloaked limestone towers, glass-clear lagoons you paddle into by kayak, and white beaches with only your footprints on them. You swim beside wild sea turtles and rare dugongs, then watch the sun sink behind a pyramid-shaped island.

weather.note: Dry, breezy season. Bikini weather every single day.

why.animals: Snorkel above wild green and hawksbill turtles in Port Barton, and float quietly near endangered dugongs with a ranger in Busuanga.
why.food: Pick-your-own lobster or chilli crab, zesty kinilaw (Filipino ceviche), grilled fish with ice-cold calamansi juice, and mango everything.
why.adventure: Kayak into the Big Lagoon, cross a hanging bridge on a limestone cliff, scooter the coast road to a 4 km wild beach, swim over a WWII shipwreck, and finish in a 39°C saltwater hot spring under the stars.

highlights.title: Kayak into the Big Lagoon
highlights.hook: Paddle a narrow channel into an emerald bowl ringed by 100 m limestone walls. No motors allowed.

highlights.title: Pinagbuyutan, the pyramid in the sea
highlights.hook: A sheer cone of jungle and rock with a crescent beach at its feet, plus coral right off the sand.

highlights.title: Swimming with sea turtles
highlights.hook: Wild turtles graze the seagrass 2–3 m below you and come up to breathe right beside you.

highlights.title: Dugongs & a surreal island savanna
highlights.hook: Snorkel near gentle sea cows in Tagbanwa waters, then spot giraffes, zebras and rare Calamian deer on Calauit.

highlights.title: Kayangan Lake & the WWII wrecks
highlights.hook: The Philippines' most famous viewpoint, then snorkel over a Japanese wreck only 5 m down.

highlights.title: Scooter to Nacpan for sunset
highlights.hook: 17 km of coast road to 4 km of palm-backed sand facing the open horizon.

days.title: Wheels up
do: Long-haul flight towards Manila
Films, sleep, cosy socks
days.tip: Switch your watch to Manila time (+6 h) as soon as you board.

days.title: Hello, Philippines
do: Land in Manila, short hop to Puerto Princesa
Swim, nap, shake off the flight
Optional: evening firefly cruise through the mangroves
days.animal: Fireflies twinkling in the mangroves like Christmas lights
days.taste: Grilled fish and an ice-cold calamansi juice
days.tip: Keep this day gentle. Tomorrow the island begins.

days.title: Road trip to the slow coast
do: Drive north through jungle and rice fields (~3 h)
Barefoot afternoon on the bay
Sunset on beanbags at a beach bar
days.taste: Tacos and seared tuna in a lantern-lit jungle-garden bar
days.tip: Port Barton runs on cash. ATMs are unreliable.

days.title: Turtle day
do: Private boat to Turtle Spot first thing, while the water is glassy
Snorkel the coral gardens of Twin Reef
Lazy beach hours on a tiny island
days.animal: Wild green and hawksbill turtles grazing seagrass right beneath you
days.taste: Pistachio gelato in town, then pasta by the beach
days.tip: Go early on a private boat: fewer swimmers, calmer turtles. Look, don't touch.

days.title: Waterfall, then north
do: Morning jungle hike to Pamuayan Falls for a swim
Drive north to El Nido (~3 h)
First sunset on Las Cabanas with islands in silhouette
days.taste: Kinilaw (fresh ceviche), then sunset tapas on the beach
days.tip: The pyramid island shows its classic profile from this coast at sunset.

days.title: Into the Big Lagoon
do: Island tour A: kayak deep into the Big Lagoon
Squeeze through a rock hole into the Secret Lagoon
Snorkel Shimizu Island and 7 Commandos Beach
days.animal: Clouds of reef fish at Shimizu, sometimes a turtle cruising by
days.taste: Beach BBQ lunch, then wood-oven pizza
days.tip: Lagoon slots are capped daily, so they get pre-registered. The deeper you paddle, the quieter it gets.

days.title: Cliffs and the coast road
do: Taraw Cliff canopy walk: helmets, hanging bridge, limestone scrambles
Scooter 17 km north to Nacpan Beach
Walk the headland to wild Calitang cove
Open-sea sunset on deckchairs
days.taste: Grilled seafood at a beach shack, sunset cocktails
days.tip: Ride home before full dark. The last stretch is gravel.

days.title: Just the two of us
do: Private boat, island tour B
Walk the curving Snake Island sandbar at low tide
Picnic and snorkel under the Pinagbuyutan pyramid
Slow ride home through golden hour
days.animal: Coral and reef fish just off Pinagbuyutan's beach
days.taste: A picnic on the boat under the Pinagbuyutan pyramid, then sunset behind the islands
days.tip: The romantic one. The crew times the return for sunset.

days.title: Crossing to Coron
do: Morning fast ferry across the sea (~4 h)
Climb Mt Tapyas's 721 steps for sunset over the islands
Soak in the 39°C Maquinit saltwater hot spring after dark
days.taste: Pick-your-own lobster or chilli crab
days.tip: Take seasickness tablets. There's a short flight if the sea says no.

days.title: Lakes of Coron Island
do: 7:00 at Kayangan Lake: climb to the postcard viewpoint, then swim
Swim through the rock gap into Twin Lagoon
Barracuda Lake's warm and cool water layers
Snorkel the Skeleton Wreck
days.animal: Silver fish in Barracuda Lake, maybe a turtle at Siete Pecados reef
days.taste: Lunch cooked on the boat, ribs in town
days.tip: The lakes are sacred to the Tagbanwa people. Life vests on, voices low.

days.title: Dugongs and giraffes
do: 5:00 start across Busuanga by road and boat
Ranger-led dugong snorkel: small groups, 15 minutes in the water, 5 m distance
Calauit by jeep: giraffes, zebras and endemic Calamian deer
days.animal: A dugong gliding over seagrass. The main event.
days.taste: Packed lunch on the boat, rooftop cocktails at night
days.tip: We say no to giraffe hand-feeding and just watch. Sightings of dugongs happen on about 2 in 3 trips.

days.title: Wrecks and white sand
do: Snorkel the Lusong Gunboat wreck (or dive the WWII wrecks)
Afternoon on a quiet white island beach like Malcapuya
days.animal: Reef fish sheltering among the wrecks
days.taste: Farewell tapas and wine at Coron's one proper wine bar
days.tip: This doubles as a spare day if wind cancels the dugong trip.

days.title: Homeward, sun-kissed
do: Morning market stroll for mangoes
Island hop to Manila, then home for Christmas
days.taste: One last mango shake
days.tip: Home in time for Christmas, very tanned.

goodToKnow: Dry northeast-monsoon season: hot, breezy, some afternoon chop on open water.
Ethical only: no Oslob whale-shark feeding, no animal feeding anywhere.
We skip the crowded Underground River. Turtles beat it.

name: Tenerife
tagline: One island, two moods, a billion stars
summary: Two islands in one: a sunny south where pilot whales live just offshore beneath 600 m sea cliffs, and a lush green north of cloud forests, black-sand coves and volcanic vineyards. In between rises Teide, and above it one of the clearest night skies on Earth.

weather.note: Shorts and tees by the sea, a fleece for the volcano at night.

wrap.tagHint: volcanoes & a sky full of stars

why.animals: Wild pilot whales and dolphins that live here all year, watched from small licensed boats at a respectful 60 m, with no tanks and no shows. Plus birds found nowhere else on Earth, like the Tenerife blue chaffinch.
why.food: We'd be there in guachinche season, when farm families open their homes to pour their own new wine next to papas arrugadas and mojo. Volcanic-slope tastings with island cheeses, 600 m above the Atlantic.
why.adventure: Kayak under the Los Gigantes cliffs, hike volcanic moonscapes and mossy laurel forest, and drive the hairpin road to Masca. Every day ends with a different sunset.

highlights.title: Sunset above the clouds, then the Milky Way
highlights.hook: Cable car to 3,555 m as Teide's shadow falls over a sea of clouds, then telescopes under a protected Starlight sky.

highlights.title: Pilot whales & dolphins, ethically
highlights.hook: A resident pod lives in the protected strait to La Gomera, so sightings happen all year.

highlights.title: Kayak under Los Gigantes
highlights.hook: Paddle past sea caves at the foot of 600 m cliffs, then snorkel in clear water.

highlights.title: Masca, the hidden valley
highlights.hook: A hairpin road to a hamlet clinging above a ravine, with La Gomera floating on the horizon.

highlights.title: Cloud forest to black-sand sunset
highlights.hook: Moss-draped laurel tunnels in Anaga give way to the sea stacks of Benijo at golden hour.

highlights.title: Wine country in guachinche season
highlights.hook: Tastings on volcanic slopes, then dinner where a family pours its own young wine from the jug.

days.title: Hello, sunshine
do: Land, grab the car, shorts on
Walk the black sand of Playa de la Arena
Sunset behind La Gomera from the Los Gigantes seafront
days.taste: Catch of the day with papas arrugadas and green mojo by the harbour
days.tip: Pack water shoes and reef-safe sunscreen. You'll use both all week.

days.title: The whales' backyard
do: Morning small-boat whale & dolphin trip into the protected strait (~3 h)
Lazy beach afternoon
Swim in the natural pool under the cliffs if the sea is calm
days.animal: Resident pilot whales and bottlenose dolphins, watched from 60 m with the engine quiet
days.taste: Grilled limpets and a crisp young Listán Blanco at sunset
days.tip: Only licensed 'Barco Azul' boats: no chasing, no swimming with them.

days.title: Giants and the hidden valley
do: Morning kayak under the Los Gigantes cliffs, with a snorkel stop
Road trip up the TF-436 hairpins to Masca
A barraquito (layered coffee) on a terrace above the gorge
Sunset at Mirador de Cherfe
days.animal: Dolphins or a turtle may pass the kayak. Watch, never approach.
days.taste: Barraquito, then local goat cheese with palm honey
days.tip: Feeling sporty? Swap in the Masca gorge hike down to the sea and take a boat back.

days.title: Above the clouds
days.base: Over Teide to the green north
do: Drive up through the pine forest
Hike the Roques de García loop in the volcanic caldera
Cable car at sunset to 3,555 m: Teide's shadow over a sea of clouds
Stargazing with a guide and telescopes
days.animal: The Tenerife blue chaffinch, found only on this island, visits the pond at Las Lajas
days.taste: Hot chocolate and a picnic under the Milky Way
days.tip: 25°C at the beach, near 0°C up top after dark. Bring layers.

days.title: Wine, honey and black sand
do: Sleep in
Bodega tasting on volcanic slopes: three wines with island cheeses
Casa del Vino, a 300-year-old farmhouse with a wine-and-honey museum
Late afternoon at El Bollullo, a wild black-sand cove
days.taste: Guachinche night: house wine from the jug, slow-cooked meats, papas with red mojo
days.tip: Guachinches are cash-only, Spanish-only and wonderfully chaotic.

days.title: Lava pools and a dragon tree
do: Swim in Garachico's lava-rock natural pools
Icod's thousand-year-old dragon tree
Sunset on Playa Jardín's black sand among gardens and waterfalls
days.animal: Seabirds nesting on the islet off Garachico
days.taste: Grilled parrotfish by the sea and a glass of Malvasía
days.tip: Swim the pools only when the sea is calm. On big-swell days, the waves are a show instead.

days.title: Into the cloud forest
do: Boardwalk through moss-draped laurel forest at Cruz del Carmen
Hike a ridge loop with 360° views of Anaga
Lunch in the village of Taganana
Sunset on the black sand and sea stacks of Benijo
days.animal: Listen for laurel pigeons, which live only in these ancient forests
days.taste: Fresh fish with mojo verde in a tiny seaside village
days.tip: Start early. Bring a torch for the steps back up from Benijo.

days.title: Pastel streets and a last swim
do: La Laguna's UNESCO old town of pastel mansions
Market in Santa Cruz for cheeses, fruit and flowers
Afternoon swim at golden Las Teresitas
days.taste: Farewell candlelit dinner with volcanic wines and a sweet Malvasía to finish
days.tip: Climb the Concepción tower for rooftop views.

days.title: Adiós, volcano
do: Slow breakfast and a last barraquito
Pack the bottles we loved and some island honey
days.taste: Quesadillas (sweet cheese pastries) for the road
days.tip: Leave buffer time for traffic around Santa Cruz.

goodToKnow: The north is greener and gets more showers; the south is sunnier and drier.
Teide summit and some forest trails need free permits.
Ethical only: no turtle feeding tours, no captive dolphin shows, no camel rides.

name: Cape Town
tagline: Penguins, baboons, vineyards and a safari
summary: A flat-topped mountain over a sparkling city, a wild coast where penguins waddle past swimmers and baboons patrol the cliffs, and rolling wine valleys where every tasting comes with a view. Then a road trip east to whale cliffs and a malaria-free Big 5 safari under huge Karoo skies.

weather.note: Early summer: sunny, sometimes very windy. Shorts by day, a light jacket at night.

why.animals: Wild penguins at Boulders, playful seals twirling around you off Hout Bay, baboons and ostriches at Cape Point, and free-roaming elephants, giraffes and rare white lions on safari. No petting, no shows, only wild animals.
why.food: Chocolate-and-wine pairings in Constantia, a gourmet pairing lunch in the Heaven-and-Earth valley, Cap Classique bubbly on Route 62, and a hop-on wine tram through Franschhoek's vineyards.
why.adventure: Hike Table Mountain and Lion's Head, kayak to the penguins, then drive Chapman's Peak, Clarence Drive and Route 62: three of the world's great drives on one loop.

highlights.title: Paddle to the penguins
highlights.hook: Kayak over clear water at dawn while African penguins rocket past toward their fishing grounds.

highlights.title: Snorkel with fur seals
highlights.hook: Curious young seals twirl, stare into your mask and tug your fins. Wild and fully on their terms.

highlights.title: Big 5 safari in the Karoo
highlights.hook: Free-roaming elephants, white lions, cheetah and rhino across 62,000 ha of mountains, with bush walks and starry nights.

highlights.title: Chapman's Peak at golden hour
highlights.hook: 9 km and 114 bends carved into a sheer cliff above the Atlantic.

highlights.title: Franschhoek Wine Tram
highlights.hook: Hop between historic estates for oyster, chocolate and bubbly pairings.

highlights.title: Table Mountain & Lion's Head
highlights.hook: Climb onto a 1,000 m tabletop, then watch the sun drop into the Atlantic from Lion's Head.

days.title: Hello, Mother City
do: Land, pick up the car
Sunset stroll on the Sea Point promenade
Sundowners in Camps Bay as the Twelve Apostles turn pink
days.animal: Fur seals snoozing on the harbour platforms at the Waterfront
days.taste: Seafood and a chilled Cape Chenin Blanc
days.tip: Long flight. If we land late, we just sleep.

days.title: On top of the table
do: Hike up Table Mountain (or take the rotating cable car)
Wander Bo-Kaap's candy-coloured streets
Food market afternoon
Lion's Head sunset hike
days.animal: Dassies (rock hyraxes) sunbathing on the summit rocks
days.taste: Cape Malay curry, samoosas and koeksisters in Bo-Kaap
days.tip: If the 'tablecloth' cloud is down, we swap with Day 4.

days.title: Penguins, baboons and the edge of Africa
do: Dawn sea-kayak to see penguins from the water
Boulders Beach boardwalk and a swim among the boulders
Cape of Good Hope: lighthouse and wild fynbos
Drive Chapman's Peak into the sunset
days.animal: Penguins at dawn, then chacma baboons, ostriches and eland roaming the cape
days.taste: Harbour fish and chips by False Bay
days.tip: Baboons open car doors! Windows up, food hidden, watch from a few metres.

days.title: Seals, gardens and Constantia
do: Morning seal snorkel off Hout Bay (wetsuit provided)
Kirstenbosch gardens and the treetop canopy walkway
Constantia, South Africa's oldest wine route, with a chocolate-and-wine pairing
days.animal: Wild seals pirouetting around you underwater, then sunbirds sipping from proteas
days.taste: Vin de Constance, the sweet wine Napoleon asked for in exile
days.tip: We skip the harbour 'seal men' who make seals pose for tips.

days.title: The whale coast
do: Drive cliff-hugging Clarence Drive along False Bay
Stony Point: a quiet penguin colony on a boardwalk
Walk Hermanus' 12 km clifftop path
Afternoon in the Heaven-and-Earth wine valley
days.animal: Penguins and cormorants at Stony Point, maybe a late-season whale close to the cliffs
days.taste: A food-and-wine pairing lunch among Pinot Noir vines
days.tip: Whales are leaving by now, so a sighting is a bonus, not a promise.

days.title: Two oceans and into the Karoo
do: Cape Agulhas: Africa's southernmost tip, where two oceans meet
Lunch in historic Swellendam
Tradouw Pass gorge onto Route 62
First game drive at golden hour
days.animal: First safari sighting: elephants, giraffes or the white lions
days.taste: Dinner under the stars at the reserve
days.tip: The longest driving day. Early start, full tank.

days.title: Wild Karoo
do: Dawn game drive tracking elephants, lions and cheetah
Guided bush walk to ancient San rock art
Pool and siesta in the Karoo warmth
Private sundowner with bubbly on a quiet ridge, then stargazing
days.animal: Elephants at a waterhole, the white lion pride, giraffes against the mountains
days.taste: A glass of Robertson Cap Classique as the mountains turn copper
days.tip: The romantic one. A fleece for dawn drives, a hat for midday.

days.title: Route 62 wine road
do: Last dawn game drive
Arty Barrydale and the Montagu hot springs
Sparkling-wine tasting in the Robertson valley
Golden hour in Franschhoek's vineyards
days.animal: One last safari sighting at dawn
days.taste: Cap Classique bubbles, then dinner in South Africa's gourmet village
days.tip: The driver spits, the birthday girl sips.

days.title: The wine tram
do: First wine tram departure, 3–4 estates on one line
Oyster pairing, chocolate pairing, art-and-garden estates
Long lazy vineyard lunch and an evening stroll
days.animal: One tram line stops at a wine farm with a sanctuary for rescued pigs
days.taste: Oysters with a crisp white, then bubbly
days.tip: Nobody drives today.

days.title: A farewell with a view
do: Drive the Helshoogte Pass through mountain-and-vine panoramas
Final tasting on a terrace over the Stellenbosch valley
To the airport
days.taste: A last glass with a sculpture-garden view
days.tip: Birthday bonus idea: adopt a penguin through the seabird rescue charity.

goodToKnow: The ocean is cold, around 12–18°C. Swims are short and very refreshing.
Ethical only: no cub petting, no walking with lions, no elephant rides.
Normal big-city care: nothing on car seats, hike popular trails in daylight.

name: Madeira
region: Funchal · the peaks · the wild north
tagline: Above the clouds, beside the dolphins
summary: A green volcanic island in the Atlantic where you can hike ridges above a sea of clouds, walk through fairy-tale laurel forests and swim in black lava pools, all in one day. Wild dolphins play off the south coast, and evenings mean old wine cellars and sunsets over 500 m sea cliffs.

weather.note: Sunny south, misty north. Shorts below, a fleece for the peaks.

wrap.tagHint: a fairy-tale forest in the clouds

why.animals: Wild Atlantic spotted dolphins and pilot whales live here all year, watched from small naturalist-led boats. Cows wander the misty Fanal forest, and you can snorkel with big groupers in a protected marine reserve.
why.food: Centuries-old Madeira wine in Funchal's lodges, beef skewered on laurel sticks in a vineyard with the estate's own Verdelho, and grilled limpets with poncha at sunset.
why.adventure: One short coastal road trip packs a summit ridge above the clouds, a canyoning descent through waterfalls, sea kayaking, levada trails into waterfall valleys and hairpin drives down to black-sand coves.

highlights.title: Sunrise above the clouds
highlights.hook: Watch the sun rise over a white sea of cloud at 1,818 m, then walk a knife-edge ridge to the island's highest peak.

highlights.title: Wild dolphins off Calheta
highlights.hook: Pods ride the bow, and with luck pilot whales surface right beside the boat.

highlights.title: The Fanal fog forest
highlights.hook: 500-year-old laurel trees emerge from drifting fog while cows graze between them.

highlights.title: Ponta de São Lourenço
highlights.hook: A red, ochre and black volcanic peninsula with the Atlantic on both sides. Another planet.

highlights.title: Lava pools & a vineyard feast
highlights.hook: Swim in turquoise lava-rock pools, walk black sand, then lunch among the vines.

highlights.title: Glass cable car & wicker toboggan
highlights.hook: Fly up to Monte over a glass floor, then slide back down in a basket steered by men in straw hats.

days.title: Hello, Atlantic
do: Land, grab the car, 20 minutes to Funchal
Old-town lanes of painted doors
Seafront sunset
days.taste: Garlic-butter limpets, bolo do caco and your first poncha
days.tip: Trail slots get booked online in advance. Save the QR codes offline.

days.title: Waterfalls and wicker sleds
do: Beginner canyoning: about 6 waterfalls, abseils and optional jumps
Glass-floored cable car up to Monte and its tropical gardens
Toboggan ride back down. Pure giggles.
days.animal: Koi ponds and lizards in the gardens
days.taste: Espetada (beef on laurel skewers) in the village where it was born
days.tip: Canyoning goes early in the trip so there's room to reschedule after rain.

days.title: Sunrise above the clouds
do: Drive up in the dark to Pico do Arieiro (1,818 m)
Sunrise over a sea of clouds
Hike the ridge to Pico Ruivo (1,862 m): tunnels, stairways, wow
Lazy afternoon by the pool
days.animal: Kestrels hovering on the updrafts
days.taste: Hot garlic bread at the summit hut, then scabbardfish with banana
days.tip: It can be 5°C at dawn. Gloves and a down layer.

days.title: The red-rock peninsula
do: Early cliff walk out to Ponta de São Lourenço
Whale Museum in Caniçal, where whalers became protectors
Afternoon on Machico's golden beach
days.animal: Lizards everywhere, seabirds riding the wind, and the rare chance of a monk seal offshore
days.taste: Fresh tuna steak in a fishing village
days.tip: No shade and strong wind: sun cream plus windbreaker.

days.title: Snorkel, skywalk, westward
do: Kayak and snorkel in the Garajau marine reserve
Step onto the Cabo Girão glass skywalk, 580 m above the sea
Poncha in the fishing harbour where it was invented
Golden hour in Calheta
days.animal: Big groupers and shoals of fish in a no-take reserve
days.taste: Scabbardfish with banana by the harbour
days.tip: Snorkel in the morning, when the sea is calmest.

days.title: Dolphins and a lighthouse sunset
do: Morning dolphin and whale watching with marine biologists
Lazy hours on Calheta's sheltered beach
Sugarcane mill: rum and honey cake
Sunset picnic at Ponta do Pargo lighthouse, 300 m above the open ocean
days.animal: Wild dolphins at the bow, maybe pilot whales, from a respectful distance
days.taste: A picnic of bolo do caco, local cheese and chilled Verdelho
days.tip: The romantic one. Stay until the stars come out.

days.title: Into the fairy forest
do: Levada walk to 25 Fontes: a mossy cirque of 25 springs
Afternoon in the Fanal laurel forest as the fog rolls in
Hairpins down to the north coast
days.animal: Cows grazing under ancient laurels, and tame chaffinches on the trail
days.taste: Grilled fish by the sea with a glass of Seixal white
days.tip: Cash and a headlamp for the trail. Don't feed the chaffinches, however cute.

days.title: Lava pools and vineyard feast
do: Morning swim in Porto Moniz's volcanic pools as waves crash around you
Seixal's black-sand beach and the Bride's Veil waterfall
Vineyard tasting and laurel-skewer lunch above São Vicente
days.animal: Rock pools full of crabs and little fish
days.taste: The estate's Verdelho and espetada, served right in the vineyard
days.tip: Ask the estate to pack a bottle for the evening.

days.title: Market morning
do: Mercado dos Lavradores: exotic fruit and flower sellers in costume
Last coffee by the marina
days.taste: Passion fruit tasting and a honey cake to take home
days.tip: Taste before you buy at the fruit stalls.

goodToKnow: Microclimates: the south is sunny, the north and the peaks can be misty. We go high early.
Popular trails now use timed online slots.
Ethical only: you can't swim with dolphins in Madeira, and that's how it should be.
